records.source: בְּ֭נִי אִם־תִּקַּ֣ח אֲמָרָ֑י וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י תִּצְפֹּ֥ן אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: My son, if you receive my sayings, and my commandments treasure up with you,
pieces: My son, if you take hold of what I say \q and hide my commands away like treasure,

L.1: My son, if you receive my sayings, \q and treasure up my commandments with you,

R.1: My son, accept what I tell you, \q and keep my commands safe inside you like treasure.

decisions.choice: if ... then: verses 1–11 are one long condition and promise
decisions.reason: The chapter is a single poem built like one sentence: "if" (verses 1–4), "then" (verses 5 and 9), and what wisdom will rescue the son from (verses 12–19). It has twenty-two verses, the number of letters in the Hebrew alphabet.

decisions.choice: treasure up: hide away for safekeeping
decisions.reason: The verb (tsaphan) means to hide something valuable. It is the word the gang used for lying hidden in ambush (1:11, 18); here the son hides his father's commands, and in verse 7 the LORD stores up wisdom for the upright.

decisions.choice: accept ... keep ... (as commands)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long chain of "if" clauses in verses 1–4 into short commands and picks up the condition again in verse 5 ("If you do this"), so that young readers can follow it.

records.heading: Wisdom is worth the search

records.source: לְהַקְשִׁ֣יב לַֽחָכְמָ֣ה אָזְנֶ֑ךָ תַּטֶּ֥ה לִ֝בְּךָ֗ לַתְּבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: making attentive to wisdom your ear; you incline your heart to understanding,
pieces: so that your ear is tuned to wisdom \q and your heart leans toward understanding;

L.2: making your ear attentive to wisdom, \q inclining your heart to understanding;

R.2: Listen carefully to wisdom. \q Try hard to understand.

decisions.choice: heart: the mind and will
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and decides, not chiefly where they feel (3:1; 4:23). To incline the heart is to set the mind on something.

records.source: כִּ֤י אִ֣ם לַבִּינָ֣ה תִקְרָ֑א לַ֝תְּבוּנָ֗ה תִּתֵּ֥ן קוֹלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: indeed, if for discernment you call, for understanding you give your voice,
pieces: if you truly cry out for insight \q and raise your voice to call for understanding,

L.3: yes, if you call out for discernment, \q [and] give your voice for understanding,

R.3: Call out for good sense. \q Shout for understanding.

decisions.choice: indeed, if: a stronger form of the condition
decisions.reason: The pair of words (ki im) raises the stakes: not only listening (verse 2) but calling out.

decisions.choice: call ... give your voice: answering Wisdom's call
decisions.reason: These are the verbs used of Wisdom in 1:20–21: she "gives her voice" and "calls". Now the son is to call out for her as she called out for him.

records.source: אִם־תְּבַקְשֶׁ֥נָּה כַכָּ֑סֶף וְֽכַמַּטְמוֹנִ֥ים תַּחְפְּשֶֽׂנָּה׃
records.gloss: if you seek it like silver, and like hidden treasures search for it,
pieces: if you go looking for it as you would for silver, \q and hunt for it as for buried treasure,

L.4: if you seek it like silver, \q and like hidden treasures search for it,

R.4: Look for wisdom the way you would look for silver or hidden treasure.

decisions.choice: silver ... hidden treasures: dug out with great effort
decisions.reason: Silver was mined from deep in the ground (Job 28:1–11), and valuables were buried for safety (Jeremiah 41:8). Finding wisdom takes the same effort, and it is worth more (3:14; 8:19).

records.source: אָ֗ז תָּ֭בִין יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת אֱלֹהִ֣ים תִּמְצָֽא׃
records.gloss: Then you will understand [the] fear of YHWH, and [the] knowledge of God you will find.
pieces: then you will come to see what the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is, \q and you will discover what it is to know God.

L.5: then you will understand the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and the knowledge of God you will find.

R.5: If you do this, you will understand what it means to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe. \q You will come to know God.

decisions.choice: the knowledge of God: knowing God
decisions.reason: The phrase means coming to know God, as in Hosea 4:1 and 6:6, not the knowledge God has.

decisions.choice: the fear of the LORD: the goal of the search
decisions.reason: In 1:7 the fear of the LORD is where knowledge begins. Here it is also what the search arrives at: reverence for God is both the start and the end of wisdom.

decisions.choice: what it is to know God
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the phrase means (m1), since "the knowledge of God" can be read as knowledge that God has.

records.source: כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יִתֵּ֣ן חָכְמָ֑ה מִ֝פִּ֗יו דַּ֣עַת וּתְבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: For YHWH gives wisdom; from his mouth [are] knowledge and understanding.
pieces: For it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who gives wisdom; \q knowledge and understanding come from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth.

L.6: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives wisdom; \q from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth [come] knowledge and understanding.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who gives wisdom. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks, people come to know and understand.

decisions.choice: the LORD gives wisdom: what is searched for is also a gift
decisions.reason: The son must search hard (verses 1–4), yet wisdom is the LORD's gift, as it was to Solomon (1 Kings 3:9–12). The two belong together.

decisions.choice: from his mouth: by what he says
decisions.reason: Knowledge comes from the LORD's word, as the father's teaching comes from his (verse 1).

records.source: יִצְפֹּ֣ן לַ֭יְשָׁרִים תּוּשִׁיָּ֑ה מָ֝גֵ֗ן לְהֹ֣לְכֵי תֹֽם׃
records.gloss: And he stores up for the upright sound wisdom, a shield for those walking [in] integrity,
pieces: He keeps sound wisdom in reserve for the upright; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shields those who live with integrity,

L.7: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright, \q a shield for those who walk [in] integrity,

R.7: He saves up good sense for people who do what is right. \q He protects people who live honestly, like a shield.

decisions.choice: he stores up, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: and he has stored up (the written form)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) give a different form of the verb from the reading the scribes marked for it (qere). The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: sound wisdom: practical wisdom that succeeds
decisions.reason: The word (tushiyyah) means wisdom that works, and so also the success it brings (3:21; 8:14; Job 26:3).

decisions.choice: a shield: protection
decisions.reason: The LORD as a shield is a common picture of his protection (Genesis 15:1; Psalm 3:4; Proverbs 30:5).

records.source: לִ֭נְצֹר אָרְח֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וְדֶ֖רֶךְ חֲסִידָ֣יו יִשְׁמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: guarding [the] paths of justice, and [the] way of his faithful ones he keeps.
pieces: watching over the paths of justice \q and protecting the way of those who are loyal to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.8: guarding the paths of justice, \q and the way of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps.

R.8: He watches over people who are fair to others, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keeps safe those who are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: his faithful ones: those who are loyal to him
decisions.reason: The word (hasid) comes from hesed, faithful love. It names people who keep faith with God (Psalm 4:4; 30:5).

decisions.choice: the paths of justice: the paths of those who act justly
decisions.reason: The parallel line ("the way of his faithful ones") shows that the paths are those of people who do what is just.

records.source: אָ֗ז תָּ֭בִין צֶ֣דֶק וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מֵישָׁרִ֗ים כָּל־מַעְגַּל־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: Then you will understand righteousness and justice and uprightness, every track of good.
pieces: Then you will understand righteousness, justice and fairness, \q and every good road to take.

L.9: Then you will understand righteousness and justice \q and uprightness, every good track.

R.9: Then you will understand what is right, fair and honest. \q You will know the good way to live.

decisions.choice: righteousness, justice and uprightness: as in 1:3
decisions.reason: The same three words name the purpose of the book in 1:3. The "then" here picks up verse 5: the son will understand God (verse 5) and right living (verse 9).

decisions.choice: track: a worn road
decisions.reason: The word (magal) is a track worn by wheels, a well-used way (4:11, 26).

records.source: כִּֽי־תָב֣וֹא חָכְמָ֣ה בְלִבֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝דַ֗עַת לְֽנַפְשְׁךָ֥ יִנְעָֽם׃
records.gloss: For wisdom will come into your heart, and knowledge to your soul will be pleasant;
pieces: For wisdom will come into your heart, \q and knowing will become a delight to you.

L.10: For wisdom will come into your heart, \q and knowledge to your soul will be pleasant;

R.10: Wisdom will become part of you, \q and you will enjoy learning.

decisions.choice: soul: your whole self
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) is the living person, with all their desires (as in 1:18–19). Knowledge will be something the son enjoys, not a burden.

decisions.choice: will become a delight to you
alternatives: will be pleasant to your soul
decisions.reason: Balanced says "to you", since "soul" in English suggests only the spiritual part of a person (m1).

records.source: מְ֭זִמָּה תִּשְׁמֹ֥ר עָלֶ֗יךָ תְּבוּנָ֥ה תִנְצְרֶֽכָּה׃
records.gloss: discretion will watch over you; understanding will guard you,
pieces: foresight will stand guard over you, \q and understanding will keep you safe,

L.11: discretion will watch over you; \q understanding will guard you,

R.11: Good sense will protect you. \q Understanding will keep you safe.

decisions.choice: discretion: the ability to plan and think ahead
decisions.reason: The word (mezimmah) is the one in 1:4. The faculties the son has gained now guard him like sentries.

records.source: לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ רָ֑ע מֵ֝אִ֗ישׁ מְדַבֵּ֥ר תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: to deliver you from [the] way of evil, from [a] man speaking perverse things,
pieces: rescuing you from the road of evil, \q from people whose speech twists the truth,

L.12: to deliver you from [the] way of evil, \q from {{gender:a person|a man}} speaking perverse things,

R.12: Wisdom will save you from the way of evil people. \q It will save you from people who say twisted things.

decisions.choice: perverse things: words that turn things upside down
decisions.reason: The word (tahpukot) comes from a root meaning to overturn. It is speech that turns good into bad and truth into lies (8:13; 10:31–32).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone, though the singular stands for a whole group
decisions.reason: The singular "man" (ish) is followed by plural verbs in verses 13–15, so it stands for a kind of person, as in the gang of 1:10–19.

records.source: הַ֭עֹ֣זְבִים אָרְח֣וֹת יֹ֑שֶׁר לָ֝לֶ֗כֶת בְּדַרְכֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: those leaving paths of uprightness to walk in ways of darkness,
pieces: who desert the honest road \q to go walking down dark ways,

L.13: those leaving [the] paths of uprightness \q to walk in [the] ways of darkness,

R.13: They have stopped doing what is right and now live in darkness.

decisions.choice: ways of darkness: evil and ignorance
decisions.reason: The path of the wicked is dark, and they cannot see what trips them (4:19), while the path of the righteous grows brighter (4:18).

records.source: הַ֭שְּׂמֵחִים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָ֑ע יָ֝גִ֗ילוּ בְּֽתַהְפֻּכ֥וֹת רָֽע׃
records.gloss: the ones rejoicing to do evil; they exult in perversities of evil,
pieces: who enjoy doing wrong \q and celebrate the twisted ways of evil,

L.14: who rejoice in doing evil \q [and] exult in [the] perversities of evil,

R.14: They are happy when they do wrong. \q They love the twisted things evil people do.

decisions.choice: rejoice ... exult: take pleasure in
decisions.reason: Both words are words for joy, used here of joy in the wrong thing (contrast 10:23; 15:21).

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָרְחֹתֵיהֶ֣ם עִקְּשִׁ֑ים וּ֝נְלוֹזִ֗ים בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: whose paths [are] crooked, and devious in their tracks.
pieces: people whose roads wind and twist, \q who go astray at every turn.

L.15: whose paths [are] crooked, \q and [who are] devious in their tracks,

R.15: The way they live is crooked, \q and they cannot be trusted.

decisions.choice: crooked ... devious: bent and turning aside
decisions.reason: The first word (iqqesh) means twisted; the second (luz) means turning aside (3:32; 14:2). Their lives are the opposite of the straight paths of verse 13.

records.source: לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה׃
records.gloss: to deliver you from [the] strange woman, from [the] foreign woman [who] makes smooth her sayings,
pieces: It will also rescue you from the woman who is not yours to have, \q the stranger whose words are smooth and flattering,

L.16: to deliver you from [the] strange woman, \q from [the] foreign woman [who] makes her sayings smooth,

R.16: Wisdom will also save you from a woman who is married to another man \q and tries to tempt you with sweet talk.

decisions.choice: strange ... foreign: a woman outside the bounds of the son's marriage
decisions.reason: The two words (zarah, nokriyyah) mean someone who does not belong, an outsider. They can mean a foreigner, but verse 17 shows she is a wife who has left her husband. What makes her "strange" is that she is not the son's to have (5:15–20; 6:26; 7:19).

decisions.choice: makes her sayings smooth: flatters
decisions.reason: Smooth words are flattering and deceptive (5:3; 7:5, 21; Psalm 5:10).

decisions.choice: a woman who is married to another man
decisions.reason: Readable draws on verse 17 to say who she is (m1).

records.source: הַ֭עֹזֶבֶת אַלּ֣וּף נְעוּרֶ֑יהָ וְאֶת־בְּרִ֖ית אֱלֹהֶ֣יהָ שָׁכֵֽחָה׃
records.gloss: who leaves [the] companion of her youth, and [the] covenant of her God she has forgotten;
pieces: who has turned her back on the man she married when young, \q and let the covenant of her God slip from her mind.

L.17: who leaves the companion of her youth, \q and the covenant of her God she has forgotten;

R.17: She has left her husband \q and forgotten the promise she made in front of God.

decisions.choice: companion of her youth: her husband
decisions.reason: The word (alluph) means a close friend (16:28; Jeremiah 3:4). With "of her youth" it is the husband she married when young (Malachi 2:14–15).

decisions.choice: the covenant of her God: her marriage, made before God
alternatives: God's covenant with Israel, which forbids adultery
decisions.reason: Malachi 2:14 calls a wife "the wife of your covenant", with the LORD as witness. The phrase may instead mean the covenant at Sinai, whose law she breaks (Exodus 20:14). Either way, leaving her husband is unfaithfulness to God.

decisions.choice: the promise she made in front of God
decisions.reason: Readable follows the first reading (m2) and uses a plain word for covenant.

records.source: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה אֶל־מָ֣וֶת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְאֶל־רְ֝פָאִ֗ים מַעְגְּלֹתֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: for she sinks down to death [—] her house, and to the shades her tracks.
pieces: Her house slides down into death, \q and her paths end among the dead.

L.18: for her house sinks down to death, \q and her tracks to the shades;

R.18: Going to her house is like walking down the road to death. \q Her paths lead to the grave.

decisions.choice: her house sinks down to death
alternatives: she sinks down to death, (and) her house
her path sinks down to death
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine but "house" is masculine, so the line is hard. It may say that she herself sinks down, or a small change gives "her path". The sense is clear either way: going to her house is going down to death (7:27; 9:18).

decisions.choice: the shades: the dead in Sheol
decisions.reason: The word (rephaim) names the dead as weak shadows in the underworld (9:18; 21:16; Isaiah 14:9). Elsewhere it is the name of an ancient people (Deuteronomy 2:11).

decisions.choice: the shades
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the old word for the ghostly dead; Balanced and Readable say "the dead" and "the grave".

records.source: כָּל־בָּ֭אֶיהָ לֹ֣א יְשׁוּב֑וּן וְלֹֽא־יַ֝שִּׂ֗יגוּ אָרְח֥וֹת חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: All going to her will not return, and will not reach paths of life.
pieces: None who go in to her ever come back, \q nor do they reach the paths of life again.

L.19: All who go to her will not return, \q and will not reach [the] paths of life.

R.19: Men who go to her never come back. \q They never find the road that leads to life.

decisions.choice: go to her: have sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual union (Genesis 16:2; 30:3).

decisions.choice: will not return: cannot find the way back
decisions.reason: The picture follows from verse 18: her house is a road down to the dead, and no one comes back up from there (Job 7:9–10).

records.source: לְמַ֗עַן תֵּ֭לֵךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ טוֹבִ֑ים וְאָרְח֖וֹת צַדִּיקִ֣ים תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: So that you may walk in [the] way of good [people], and [the] paths of righteous [people] you will keep.
pieces: So you will go the way good people go \q and stay on the paths of the righteous.

L.20: So you will walk in the way of [the] good, \q and the paths of [the] righteous you will keep.

R.20: So you will live the way good people live, \q and you will follow the ways of those who do what is right.

decisions.choice: so that: the goal of the whole poem
decisions.reason: The word (lemaan) gives the purpose of everything from verse 1: wisdom is sought, and rescues, so that the son will walk with the good.

records.source: כִּֽי־יְשָׁרִ֥ים יִשְׁכְּנוּאָ֑רֶץ וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים יִוָּ֥תְרוּ בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For [the] upright will dwell [in the] land, and [the] blameless will remain in it,
pieces: For it is the upright who will live in the land, \q and those with integrity who will remain there,

L.21: For [the] upright will dwell [in the] land, \q and [the] blameless will be left in it;

R.21: People who do right will live in the land, \q and people who are honest will stay there.

decisions.choice: the land: the land God gave Israel
decisions.reason: The word (erets) can mean the earth, but here it is the land promised to Israel, where the faithful live and the wicked are cut off (10:30; Psalm 37:9, 11, 29; Deuteronomy 28:63).

decisions.choice: blameless: whole, with integrity
decisions.reason: The word (tamim) means whole or complete, not perfect. The gang used it of swallowing victims "whole" (1:12).

records.source: וּ֭רְשָׁעִים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יִכָּרֵ֑תוּ וּ֝בוֹגְדִ֗ים יִסְּח֥וּ מִמֶּֽנָּה׃פ
records.gloss: but [the] wicked from [the] land will be cut off, and [the] treacherous will be torn away from it.
pieces: but the wicked will be removed from the land, \q and the treacherous will be uprooted from it.

L.22: but [the] wicked from [the] land will be cut off, \q and [the] treacherous will be torn away from it.

R.22: But evil people will be removed from the land. \q People who cannot be trusted will be pulled out of it like plants.

decisions.choice: will be torn away: an active verb with no named subject
decisions.reason: The verb is active ("they will tear away") without saying who does it, a Hebrew way of saying that it will be done, by whoever does it. Behind it is the LORD's judgment (Deuteronomy 28:63).

decisions.choice: the treacherous: those who break faith
decisions.reason: The word (bogedim) is used of breaking faith with a partner or with God (Jeremiah 3:20; Malachi 2:14), as the woman of verse 17 did.

decisions.choice: pulled out of it like plants
decisions.reason: The verb is used for pulling up plants by the roots (Deuteronomy 28:63; Psalm 52:7). Readable adds "like plants" to show the picture.
